title: San Diego Wave place US forward Catarina Macario on season-ending injury list with knee injury
content:
Nearly six months after signing Catarina Macario to a historic multi-million-dollar contract, the San Diego Wave announced on Monday that they have placed the U.S. women’s national team forward on the NWSL’s season-ending injury list to continue rehabilitation for an “ongoing knee injury”.

The 26-year-old joined her hometown NWSL club in March on a contract through 2030 but has yet to feature for the club due to injury. Her contract is reportedly worth about $8 million over five years, with the Wave calling it “one of the largest contracts in women’s soccer history” when she arrived from Chelsea for a $300,000 transfer fee.

“We made a significant long-term commitment to Cat because we believe in her ability to make a lasting impact on this club,” Camille Ashton, the club’s general manager and sporting director, said in a team statement. “While we are disappointed that she will not be available this season, we are focused on her health and on supporting her throughout this process.”

When Macario first joined San Diego, it was understood she would not immediately feature for the club because she was recovering from a foot injury that sidelined her at Chelsea for several months. She remained sidelined, however, upon arriving in the NWSL and has been repeatedly listed on league availability reports as “out” for a heel injury, including most recently on Sept. 11 for the team’s match against North Carolina Courage.

A source with ties to the club confirmed to The Athletic that the forward was initially sidelined for a heel injury but later underwent a minor procedure to address an ongoing issue with her knee. The latter will sideline her for the remainder of the season.

“I’m obviously disappointed that I won’t have the opportunity to represent the club on the field this season, especially with how much it means to me to be back home in San Diego,” Macario said in the club statement. “But the club and I have made a long-term commitment to each other and are focused on the big picture. My focus is on continuing my recovery so that when I do return, I can feel like myself again and give the team and our fans the best version of me.”

By placing Macario on the league’s SEI list, the club gains access to certain roster relief measures by the NWSL, allowing the team flexibility in a player’s absence. Last week, the Wave also acquired 35-year-old Juventus forward Barbara Bonansea on a season-long loan until June 2027, likely to help balance the roster in the forward role with players like Macario and teammate Dudinha now both out on SEI.

Macario has not featured for club or country since December. The Wave said additional updates regarding her recovery “will be provided by the club when appropriate”.

San Diego fans will have to wait until at least next season to see Macario playing in a Wave kit. She has made 105 professional appearances across all competitions, scoring 44 goals and winning nine major trophies in that time. Last year, she was the U.S. women’s top goal scorer. With 29 national team caps, she has tallied 16 goals and 5 assists.

“I’m still very young in my career, and I still have so much more to give,” she told The Athletic in March, after signing with the Wave. “This next chapter will, of course, be challenging, the way that I have to get used to the league and used to the team, but I think that being home will help bring a different level to my game. I wanted a different challenge, and being able to represent my city — there’s nothing better.”

With the World Cup arriving in Brazil, the country of her birth, next summer, her recovery will be pivotal in preparing for this next chapter, too.
